# University of West Bohemia / New Technologies — Research Centre (NTC)

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | Czech Republic |
| **City** | Pilsen |
| **Tier** | Core (Tier I) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | Metrology — semitransparent / layered systems |
| **Relevant unit** | **Photo-thermal properties laboratory (NTC)** |
| **Publicly linked people** | Zdeněk Veselý |
| **Distinctive focus** | **Semitransparent coatings** — beyond opaque-body assumptions |

## Why it matters internationally

NTC extends emissivity metrology **beyond ideal opaque bulk samples** toward
technologically realistic layered and partially transmitting systems. Such
systems undermine the simple opaque-body assumptions that underwrite much
textbook emissivity thinking. A direct radiometric method for spectral
emissivity of **semitransparent coatings** has been developed at NTC, and
the institutional page explicitly lists transmittance, reflectance,
emissivity, absorptivity, and thermal conductivity among the measured
properties.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant unit

- **Photo-thermal properties laboratory (NTC)** — dedicated laboratory
  equipment for photo-thermal properties, including research on radiative
  heat transfer and direct radiometric methods tailored to semitransparent
  samples.

### Radiative properties measured

Transmittance · reflectance · emissivity · absorptivity · (coupled with)
thermal conductivity.

### Capability envelope

- **Temperature:** both low- and high-temperature work documented.
- **Methodology:** direct radiometric method for spectral emissivity of
  semitransparent coatings; laboratory equipment for photo-thermal
  properties; research on radiative heat transfer in realistic layered
  systems.

### Application domains

- Coatings — semitransparent and layered systems
- Radiative heat transfer in technologically realistic systems
- Windows, glazings, and thin-film systems that violate the opaque
  assumption

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- **Zdeněk Veselý** — photo-thermal properties measurement of coatings at
  low and high temperatures.

## Why UWB / NTC is a reference pole

Most classical emissivity methodology silently assumes the sample is opaque.
Once coatings, thin films, or transparent substrates enter the picture, that
assumption fails, and apparent emissivity becomes a complicated function of
the underlying stack. NTC is one of the laboratories that confronts this
regime head-on and has developed a documented direct radiometric method for
semitransparent coatings — placing it in a strategically important niche
between measurement science and real-world thermal-coating engineering.
